hints: Look at the steepness (gradient) of the curve, since a steeper slope means a faster rate of hydrogen production.
Notice the rate speeds up from P to Q even though reactants are being used, so think about what the exothermic heat release does to temperature and particle energy.
Remember magnesium is in large excess, so ask yourself which reactant must actually run out to make the curve flatten toward R.
walkthrough:
**Read the rate from the graph**

The gradient of a volume against time graph equals the rate of reaction. From P to Q the curve gets steeper, so rate is increasing. From Q to R the curve flattens, so rate is decreasing to zero.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{Mg(s)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_{2}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}$$

**Explain the speed-up between P and Q**

Normally rate falls as reactants are used up. Here it increases, so something must be speeding particles up. The question tells us the reaction is exothermic, so released heat raises the temperature, giving more frequent and more energetic collisions.

Rate effect:
$$\text{higher } T \rightarrow \text{more particles with } E \ge E_a \rightarrow \text{faster rate}$$

**Explain the slow-down between Q and R**

The question states a large excess of magnesium is used. That means magnesium cannot run out, so the acid must be the limiting reactant. As $\text{H}^{+}$ concentration falls, collision frequency with magnesium falls and the rate slows until the acid is used up and volume levels off.

options.A: Correct. Increasing temperature from the exothermic reaction explains the unusual increase in rate from P to Q, and falling acid concentration explains the decrease in rate from Q to R while magnesium remains in excess.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. Temperature increase correctly explains P to Q, but magnesium cannot have been used up because the question clearly states it is in large excess. The acid is limiting, not the magnesium.
options.C: Incorrect for the first part. Decreasing surface area of magnesium would slow the reaction down, not speed it up. The graph shows the rate increasing from P to Q, which needs the temperature effect.
options.D: Incorrect on both sides. Decreasing surface area would decrease rate, not increase it from P to Q, and magnesium in large excess is not used up by R. This option ignores both the exothermic heating and the excess condition.
